A region is bounded by the curve $y=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}}}$, the $x$-axis, and the lines $x=0$ and $x=\frac{3}{2}$, as shown above. Find the area $A$ of the region. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{3/2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =arccos\,(\frac{x}{3}){|}_{0}^{3/2} \\  & =arccos\,(\frac{1}{2})-arccos\,(0) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is 

$$
A=-{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{\pi }{6}.
$$
